# Physiotherapy in Kildare Town

Source: https://www.kildaredoc.ie/physiotherapy

Physiotherapy with Muqadas at Kildare Clinic on Claregate Street, Kildare Town. Call the clinic to discuss your needs and arrange a physio appointment.

## Location and contact

- Address: Claregate Street, Kildare, R51 P635, Ireland.
- Telephone: [085 867 8192](tel:+353858678192).
- Email: [info@kildaredoc.ie](mailto:info@kildaredoc.ie).
- WhatsApp: [Contact the clinic](https://wa.me/353858678192).

## Appointment hours

Physiotherapy uses the same clinic hours. Monday–Tuesday: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM. Wednesday: OFF. Thursday: 4:00 PM – 8:00 PM. Friday–Saturday: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM. Sunday: OFF. Contact the clinic to confirm current opening hours, waiting times and service availability before travelling. Confirm a physiotherapy appointment before travelling; a walk-in GP visit does not guarantee an immediately available physio slot.

## Preparing for your appointment

### Tell us what you need

Call or WhatsApp the clinic to ask about physiotherapy. Let us know whether this is your first visit or a follow-up, and confirm an appointment time before travelling.

### Prepare for your visit

Bring a list of current medicines and any relevant referral letters or reports you already have. Wear comfortable clothing that allows you to move and discuss any access needs when booking.

### Discuss a plan

A physiotherapy visit may include a conversation about your symptoms, an assessment of movement and advice about next steps. Your plan depends on your individual needs and the assessment.

## Questions

**Where can I find a physio in Kildare Town?** Kildare Clinic offers physiotherapy with Muqadas at Claregate Street, Kildare, R51 P635. Call 085 867 8192 to discuss your needs and arrange an appointment.

**How do I book a physiotherapy appointment?** Call 085 867 8192 or WhatsApp Kildare Clinic. Confirm your appointment before travelling. The clinic's walk-in GP service does not mean a physio slot is immediately available.

**Are physiotherapy hours the same as the clinic's hours?** Yes. Physiotherapy uses the same opening hours shown on this page. Contact the clinic to confirm an available appointment within those hours.

**Do I need a GP referral for physiotherapy?** Contact the clinic to confirm what is needed for your visit. If you have a referral letter or relevant reports, bring them with you. Referral requirements for an insurance claim should be checked with your insurer.

**How much does a physio appointment cost?** Contact the clinic to confirm the fee before booking. Ask whether the fee is for an initial assessment or a follow-up visit, and check any insurance requirements with your insurer.

# Kildare physio: a guide to your first appointment

Source: https://www.kildaredoc.ie/blog/kildare-physio-first-appointment

By Kildare Clinic. Published 9 October 2026.

A practical guide to choosing a physiotherapy appointment, preparing for your visit and asking the right questions at Kildare Clinic.

General information to help you plan a visit. Your clinician can advise you about your own symptoms and care.

## Finding a physio in Kildare Town

When you are looking for a Kildare physio, the most useful first step is to explain what you need help with and ask whether the service is suitable for you. Location matters, but so do appointment availability, the clinician's experience with your concern and a clear explanation of what a first visit involves.

Kildare Clinic is on Claregate Street, Kildare Town, R51 P635. Our team includes Muqadas, our physiotherapist, alongside our GPs. Contact reception to discuss a physiotherapy appointment; you can also ask which type of consultation to arrange if you are unsure.

## Should I arrange physiotherapy or see a GP?

Physiotherapy focuses on movement and physical function. An assessment can help a clinician understand how a problem affects everyday activities and discuss an appropriate plan. The right starting point depends on your symptoms and medical history.

For back pain, HSE guidance says to contact a GP if it is not improving after a few weeks, interferes with everyday activities, is very severe or is worsening. A GP may refer you to a physiotherapist or specialist. If symptoms need urgent attention, do not wait for a routine physiotherapy appointment. See the linked HSE guidance for signs that need urgent assessment.

## Questions to ask before booking

A short call can make your first visit easier to plan. Describe your concern, how long it has been present and whether you have already seen a clinician. Ask about any particular service you need rather than assuming every physiotherapy clinic offers the same treatments.

- Is this the right appointment for my concern, and who will I see?
- What times are available, and how long should I allow for the visit?
- What is the fee for an initial assessment and for follow-up visits?
- Should I bring a referral letter, medical report or anything else?
- If I plan to claim through insurance, what must I confirm with my insurer?

## How to prepare for your first appointment

Think about what you would like to get back to doing, such as being comfortable at your desk, walking further or returning to an activity. Note when your symptoms began, what seems to affect them and which everyday tasks have become difficult. This gives you a useful starting point for the conversation.

Bring your current medicine list and relevant reports or referral letters you already have. Comfortable clothing can make movement easier during an assessment. Tell reception about access needs or any questions about the visit when booking, so they can advise you before you arrive.

## What might happen during the appointment?

The clinician may ask about your concern, health history and goals, and assess how you move. They can explain their findings and discuss the next steps with you. Advice, exercises or follow-up appointments depend on the assessment; a first visit does not come with a guaranteed treatment or recovery time.

Before you leave, ask what the plan means for your usual activities, how to follow any advice safely and when to seek a further review. If an exercise or instruction is unclear, ask for an explanation. Your own plan should guide you rather than a routine copied from a general article.

## Plan your visit to Kildare Clinic

Call 085 867 8192 or WhatsApp reception to arrange physiotherapy with Muqadas. Physio appointments use the clinic's shared opening hours, listed on our physiotherapy and contact pages. Confirm a time before travelling: the walk-in GP service does not guarantee an immediately available physio appointment.

## Further information

- [HSE: Back pain — when to contact a GP](https://www2.hse.ie/conditions/back-pain/)

[Physiotherapy appointments](https://www.kildaredoc.ie/physiotherapy) | [Walk-in GP in Kildare](https://www.kildaredoc.ie/)

# Medical certificates at Kildare Clinic

Source: https://www.kildaredoc.ie/medical-certificate

Kildare Clinic offers medical certificates requested online and reviewed by Irish-registered GPs. Certificates are issued within 5 hours and only where clinically appropriate.

## Certificates and prices

- Sick Certificate: €30. An official note from a GP confirming you're unwell and unfit for work or study, for short-term minor illness.
- Unfit for Travel Certificate: €40. A GP certificate stating you are medically unfit to travel, commonly needed for airline, hotel or travel insurance claims.
- Fit to Travel Certificate: €40. A GP certificate confirming you are medically fit to travel, for airlines, tour operators or insurers that ask for one.
- Return-to-Work / Fit for Work Certificate: €30. A GP certificate confirming you have recovered and are fit to return to work or study.

## How it works

1. Send your request: Choose your certificate and fill in a short form with your details and what you need it for.
2. Pay and speak to the doctor: We email you a secure payment link, and one of our GPs calls you to verify your request.
3. Receive your certificate: Once approved, your certificate is issued and sent to you securely by email.

## Not included

- Backdated (retrospective) certificates
- Certificates that need a physical examination
- Long-term illness or detailed medical reports

## Questions

**How quickly will I receive my medical certificate?** Certificates are issued within 5 hours once the doctor has verified your request. You'll first receive a payment link by email, and a GP will call you to verify your details.

**How much does a medical certificate cost?** Sick and Return-to-Work certificates cost €30. Unfit for Travel and Fit to Travel certificates cost €40.

**Will I definitely get a certificate?** Certificates are only issued where the doctor considers it clinically appropriate. If a certificate can't be issued, the doctor will explain why and, where needed, advise you to be seen in person.

**Who reviews my request?** Every request is reviewed by an Irish-registered GP at Kildare Clinic, who will call you to verify your request before a certificate is issued.

**Can I get a backdated certificate?** No. We can't issue backdated certificates, or certificates that require a physical examination. For those, please visit the clinic during opening hours.

# Kildare Clinic cookies and browser storage

Source: https://www.kildaredoc.ie/cookies

Google Analytics and Google Maps embeds are optional. Neither loads until its separate category is allowed. Visitors can reject both, accept both or save separate preferences; Cookie settings in the footer reopens the choices. Contact details and website pages remain available when both are rejected.

## Storage

- Kildare Clinic local storage, kildare_cookie_preferences: remembers the saved analytics/maps choices and date. The choice is valid for 180 days; the browser entry remains until cleared, updated or removed by the website.
- Google Analytics cookies, _ga and _ga_*: distinguish visits and measure website use only when analytics is allowed. This website configures an expiry of up to 180 days from cookie creation and disables automatic expiry updates.
- Google Maps embed: may use Google cookies or other browser storage only after maps is allowed. Provider cookie names and durations depend on Google, account and browser settings; no complete fixed inventory is asserted.

Allowing analytics sends usage and browser/device information to Google. Loading maps sends IP address and browser information to Google. Google Fonts requests still load when optional services are rejected. Ordinary external Google Maps/WhatsApp links open those services only when followed.

## Withdrawal

Save a category as off in Cookie settings to withdraw it. Maps are removed. If analytics has started loading, site-accessible Google Analytics cookies are cleared and the page reloads to stop the tag; unsent form entries may be lost. The site cannot clear Google-domain cookies or retract data already sent.

## References

- [Google cookie information](https://policies.google.com/technologies/cookies)
- [Google cookie settings](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/guides/customize-cookies)
- [DPC cookie guidance PDF](https://www.dataprotection.ie/sites/default/files/uploads/2020-04/Guidance%20note%20on%20cookies%20and%20other%20tracking%20technologies.pdf)
